page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dasv7 server family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 16.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB per core. The processor features a 32 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on external Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression both ranking in the top tier. However, multi-threaded scaling presents a notable bottleneck; while single-threaded bzip3 decompression is in the top tier, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 25%. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth tests consistently register in the average range. For specialized workloads, the server handles small-model LLM inference and Redis SET operations at average speeds, but struggles with larger models, as evidenced by poor prompt processing performance on medium-sized LLMs.

From a resource density perspective, the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a balanced hardware profile suitable for general-purpose workloads. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs keeps the baseline resource cost aligned with standard compute needs. Given the strong single-core performance paired with average multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics, this server is well-suited for web serving, database operations, and lightweight serialization tasks, whereas highly parallelized or memory-bound computations may encounter performance limitations.

Powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, it delivers top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng and single-threaded compression benchmarks. However, multi-threaded scaling is a tradeoff, with multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth falling into average ranges, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranking in the bottom 25%. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs, relying on remote Premium Storage. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and database operations.
